By 2014 Ajax Security Team transitioned from website defacement operations to malware-based cyber espionage campaigns targeting the US defense industrial base and Iranian users of anti-censorship technologies.
Uses T1056.001 Keylogging: Ajax Security Team has used CWoolger and MPK, custom-developed malware, which recorded all keystrokes on an infected system.
Uses T1105 Ingress Tool Transfer: Ajax Security Team has used Wrapper/Gholee, custom-developed malware, which downloaded additional malware to the infected system.
Uses T1204.002 Malicious File: Ajax Security Team has lured victims into executing malicious files.
Uses T1555.003 Credentials from Web Browsers: Ajax Security Team has used FireMalv custom-developed malware, which collected passwords from the Firefox browser storage.
Uses T1566.001 Spearphishing Attachment: Ajax Security Team has used personalized spearphishing attachments.
Uses T1566.003 Spearphishing via Service: Ajax Security Team has used various social media channels to spearphish victims.

title: ATT&CK Group G1024: Akira
text:
ATT&CK Group G1024: Akira
Associated names: GOLD SAHARA, PUNK SPIDER, Howling Scorpius.
Akira is a ransomware variant and ransomware deployment entity active since at least March 2023. Akira uses compromised credentials to access single-factor external access mechanisms such as VPNs for initial access, then various publicly-available tools and techniques for lateral movement. Akira operations are associated with "double extortion" ransomware activity, where data is exfiltrated from victim environments prior to encryption, with threats to publish files if a ransom is not paid. Technical analysis of Akira ransomware indicates variants capable of targeting Windows or VMWare ESXi hypervisors and multiple overlaps with Conti ransomware.
Uses T1018 Remote System Discovery: Akira uses software such as Advanced IP Scanner and MASSCAN to identify remote hosts within victim networks.
Uses T1021.001 Remote Desktop Protocol: Akira has used RDP for lateral movement.
Uses T1027.001 Binary Padding: Akira has used binary padding to obfuscate payloads.
Uses T1036.005 Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location: Akira has used legitimate names and locations for files to evade defenses.
Uses T1059.001 PowerShell: Akira has used PowerShell scripts for credential harvesting and privilege escalation.
Uses T1078 Valid Accounts: Akira uses valid account information to remotely access victim networks, such as VPN credentials.
Uses T1133 External Remote Services: Akira uses compromised VPN accounts for initial access to victim networks.
Uses T1213.002 Sharepoint: Akira has accessed and downloaded information stored in SharePoint instances as part of data gathering and exfiltration activity.
Uses T1219 Remote Access Tools: Akira uses legitimate utilities such as AnyDesk and PuTTy for maintaining remote access to victim environments.
Uses T1482 Domain Trust Discovery: Akira uses the built-in Nltest utility or tools such as AdFind to enumerate Active Directory trusts in victim environments.
Uses T1486 Data Encrypted for Impact: Akira encrypts files in victim environments as part of ransomware operations.

title: ATT&CK Group G1024: Akira
text:
ATT&CK Group G1024: Akira
Uses T1531 Account Access Removal: Akira deletes administrator accounts in victim networks prior to encryption.
Uses T1558 Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets: Akira have used scripts to dump Kerberos authentication credentials.
Uses T1560.001 Archive via Utility: Akira uses utilities such as WinRAR to archive data prior to exfiltration.
Uses T1562.001 Disable or Modify Tools: Akira has disabled or modified security tools for defense evasion.
Uses T1567.002 Exfiltration to Cloud Storage: Akira will exfiltrate victim data using applications such as Rclone.
Uses T1657 Financial Theft: Akira engages in double-extortion ransomware, exfiltrating files then encrypting them, in order to prompt victims to pay a ransom.

title: ATT&CK Group G0129: Mustang Panda
text:
ATT&CK Group G0129: Mustang Panda
Associated names: TA416, RedDelta, BRONZE PRESIDENT, STATELY TAURUS, FIREANT, CAMARO DRAGON, EARTH PRETA, HIVE0154, TWILL TYPHOON, TANTALUM, LUMINOUS MOTH, UNC6384, TEMP.Hex, Red Lich.
Mustang Panda is a China-based cyber espionage threat actor that has been conducting operations since at least 2012. Mustang Panda has been known to use tailored phishing lures and decoy documents to deliver malicious payloads. Mustang Panda has targeted government, diplomatic, and non-governmental organizations, including think tanks, religious institutions, and research entities, across the United States, Europe, and Asia, with notable activity in Russia, Mongolia, Myanmar, Pakistan, and Vietnam.
Uses T1001.003 Protocol or Service Impersonation: Mustang Panda has utilized TLS record headers in network packets to impersonate various versions of TLS protocols to blend in with legitimate network traffic. Mustang Panda has used FakeTLS to communicate with its C2 servers.
Uses T1003 OS Credential Dumping: Mustang Panda utilized “Hdump” to dump credentials from memory.
Uses T1003.001 LSASS Memory: Mustang Panda has harvested credentials from memory of lssas.exe with Mimikatz.
Uses T1003.003 NTDS: Mustang Panda has used vssadmin to create a volume shadow copy and retrieve the NTDS.dit file. Mustang Panda has also used reg save on the SYSTEM file Registry location to help extract the NTDS.dit file.
Uses T1003.006 DCSync: Mustang Panda has leveraged Mimikatz DCSync feature to obtain user credentials.
Uses T1016 System Network Configuration Discovery: Mustang Panda has used ipconfig and arp to determine network configuration information. Mustang Panda has also utilized SharpNBTScan to scan the victim environment.
Uses T1018 Remote System Discovery: Mustang Panda has queried Active Directory for computers using AdFind. Mustang Panda has also utilized SharpNBTScan to scan the victim environment.

title: ATT&CK Group G0129: Mustang Panda
text:
ATT&CK Group G0129: Mustang Panda
Uses T1027 Obfuscated Files or Information: Mustang Panda has delivered initial payloads hidden using archives and encoding measures. Mustang Panda has also utilized opaque predicates in payloads to hinder analysis.
Uses T1027.007 Dynamic API Resolution: Mustang Panda has leveraged obfuscated Windows API function calls that were concealed as unique names, or hashes of the Windows API.
Uses T1027.012 LNK Icon Smuggling: Mustang Panda has utilized LNK files to hide malicious scripts for execution. Mustang Panda has also leveraged LNK files that were programmed to display a PDF icon to entice the victim to click on the file to execute an office.exe …
Uses T1027.016 Junk Code Insertion: Mustang Panda has used junk code within their DLL files to hinder analysis.
Uses T1036.005 Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location: Mustang Panda has used names like `adobeupdate.dat` and `PotPlayerDB.dat` to disguise PlugX, and a file named `OneDrive.exe` to load a Cobalt Strike payload. Mustang Panda has also masqueraded legitimate browser plugin updates to include AdobePlugins.exe.
Uses T1036.007 Double File Extension: Mustang Panda has used an additional filename extension to hide the true file type.
Uses T1036.008 Masquerade File Type: Mustang Panda has masqueraded malicious executables as legitimate files that download PlugX malware.
Uses T1041 Exfiltration Over C2 Channel: Mustang Panda has exfiltrated stolen data and files to its C2 server.
Uses T1046 Network Service Discovery: Mustang Panda has leveraged NBTscan to scan IP networks.
Uses T1047 Windows Management Instrumentation: Mustang Panda has executed PowerShell scripts via WMI.
Uses T1048.003 Exfiltration Over Unencrypted Non-C2 Protocol: Mustang Panda has used FTP to exfiltrate archive files.
Uses T1049 System Network Connections Discovery: Mustang Panda has used netstat -ano to determine network connection information.

title: ATT&CK Group G0129: Mustang Panda
text:
ATT&CK Group G0129: Mustang Panda
Uses T1052.001 Exfiltration over USB: Mustang Panda has used a customized PlugX variant which could exfiltrate documents from air-gapped networks.
Uses T1053.005 Scheduled Task: Mustang Panda has created a scheduled task to execute additional malicious software, as well as maintain persistence. Mustang Panda has also created a scheduled task that creates a reverse shell.
Uses T1057 Process Discovery: Mustang Panda has used tasklist /v to determine active process information. Mustang Panda has also used TONESHELL malware to check the process name and process path to ensure it matches the expected one prior to triggering a custom exception handler.
Uses T1059 Command and Scripting Interpreter: Mustang Panda has utilized meterpreter shellcode.
Uses T1059.001 PowerShell: Mustang Panda has used malicious PowerShell scripts to enable execution.
Uses T1059.003 Windows Command Shell: Mustang Panda has executed HTA files via cmd.exe, and used batch scripts for collection. Mustang Panda has also utilized cmd.exe to execute commands on an infected host such as `cmd.exe /c ping.exe 8.8.8.8 -n 70&&"%temp%\FontEDL.exe"`.
Uses T1059.005 Visual Basic: Mustang Panda has embedded VBScript components in LNK files to download additional files and automate collection. Mustang Panda has also used VBA macros in maldocs to execute malicious DLLs. Mustang Panda also utilized a VBS Script “autorun.vbs” that created persistence …
Uses T1059.007 JavaScript: Mustang Panda has executed a JavaScript payload utilizing wscript.exe on the endpoint.
Uses T1069.002 Domain Groups: Mustang Panda has leveraged AdFind to enumerate domain groups.
Uses T1070 Indicator Removal: Mustang Panda has deleted registry keys that store data and maintained persistence.
Uses T1070.004 File Deletion: Mustang Panda will delete their tools and files, and kill processes after their objectives are reached.

title: ATT&CK Group G0129: Mustang Panda
text:
ATT&CK Group G0129: Mustang Panda
Uses T1070.006 Timestomp: Mustang Panda has modified file timestamps from the export address table (EAT) in malware to make it difficult to identify creation times.
Uses T1071.001 Web Protocols: Mustang Panda has communicated with its C2 via HTTP POST requests.
Uses T1072 Software Deployment Tools: Mustang Panda has leveraged legitimate software tools such as AntiVirus Agents, Security Services, and App Development tools to execute scripts and to side-load dlls.
Uses T1074.001 Local Data Staging: Mustang Panda has stored collected credential files in c:\windows\temp prior to exfiltration. Mustang Panda has also stored documents for exfiltration in a hidden folder on USB drives.
Uses T1082 System Information Discovery: Mustang Panda has gathered system information using systeminfo.
Uses T1083 File and Directory Discovery: Mustang Panda has searched the entire target system for DOC, DOCX, PPT, PPTX, XLS, XLSX, and PDF files.
Uses T1087.002 Domain Account: Mustang Panda has utilized AdFind to identify domain users.
Uses T1091 Replication Through Removable Media: Mustang Panda has used a customized PlugX variant which could spread through USB connections.
Uses T1095 Non-Application Layer Protocol: Mustang Panda has utilized TCP-based reverse shells using cmd.exe.
Uses T1102 Web Service: Mustang Panda has used DropBox URLs to deliver variants of PlugX. Mustang Panda has also used Google Drive to host malicious downloads.
Uses T1105 Ingress Tool Transfer: Mustang Panda has downloaded additional executables following the initial infection stage. Mustang Panda has also leveraged Visual Studio Code `code.exe` and Dev Tunnels using `DevTunnel.exe` to propagate additional tools and payloads.
Uses T1106 Native API: Mustang Panda has used various Windows API calls during execution and defense evasion.
Uses T1119 Automated Collection: Mustang Panda used custom batch scripts to collect files automatically from a targeted system.
Uses T1129 Shared Modules: Mustang Panda has leveraged `LoadLibrary` to load DLLs.

title: ATT&CK Group G0129: Mustang Panda
text:
ATT&CK Group G0129: Mustang Panda
Uses T1140 Deobfuscate/Decode Files or Information: Mustang Panda has the ability to decrypt its payload prior to execution. Mustang Panda has also utilized RC4 encryption for malicious payloads.
Uses T1176.002 IDE Extensions: Mustang Panda has leveraged Visual Studio Code’s (VSCode) embedded reverse shell feature using the command `code.exe tunnel` to execute code and deliver additional payloads.
Uses T1203 Exploitation for Client Execution: Mustang Panda has exploited CVE-2017-0199 in Microsoft Word to execute code.
Uses T1204.001 Malicious Link: Mustang Panda has sent malicious links including links directing victims to a Google Drive folder. Mustang Panda has also utilized webpages with Javascript code that downloads malicious payloads to the victim device.
Uses T1204.002 Malicious File: Mustang Panda has sent malicious files requiring direct victim interaction to execute. Mustang Panda has also leveraged executable files that display decoy documents to the victim to provide a resemblance of legitimacy with customized themes related to the victim.
Uses T1205 Traffic Signaling: Mustang Panda has utilized a "magic packet" value in C2 communications and only executes in memory when response packets match specific values of “17 03 03” or “46 77 4d”.
Uses T1218.004 InstallUtil: Mustang Panda has used InstallUtil.exe to execute a malicious Beacon stager.
Uses T1218.005 Mshta: Mustang Panda has used mshta.exe to launch collection scripts.
Uses T1219.001 IDE Tunneling: Mustang Panda has utilized an established Github account to create a tunnel within the victim environment using Visual Studio Code through the `code.exe tunnel` command.
Uses T1219.002 Remote Desktop Software: Mustang Panda has installed TeamViewer on targeted systems.
Uses T1505.003 Web Shell: Mustang Panda has used China Chopper web shells to maintain access to victims’ environments.
Uses T1518 Software Discovery: Mustang Panda has searched the victim system for the InstallUtil.exe program and its version.

title: ATT&CK Group G0129: Mustang Panda
text:
ATT&CK Group G0129: Mustang Panda
Uses T1546.003 Windows Management Instrumentation Event Subscription: Mustang Panda's custom ORat tool uses a WMI event consumer to maintain persistence.
Uses T1547.001 Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder: Mustang Panda has created the registry key HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Wow6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run\AdobelmdyU to maintain persistence. Mustang Panda has also established persistence via the registry key `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run`.
Uses T1553.002 Code Signing: Mustang Panda has used valid legitimate digital signatures and certificates to evade detection.
Uses T1557 Adversary-in-the-Middle: Mustang Panda leveraged a captive portal hijack that redirected the victim to a webpage that prompted the victim to download a malicious payload.
Uses T1560.001 Archive via Utility: Mustang Panda has used RAR to create password-protected archives of collected documents prior to exfiltration. Mustang Panda has used WinRAR “Rar.exe” to archive stolen files before exfiltration. Mustang Panda has also used TONESHELL and post-exploitation tools such as RemCom and …
Uses T1560.003 Archive via Custom Method: Mustang Panda has encrypted documents with RC4 prior to exfiltration.
Uses T1564.001 Hidden Files and Directories: Mustang Panda's PlugX variant has created a hidden folder on USB drives named RECYCLE.BIN to store malicious executables and collected data. Mustang Panda has also modified file attributes to `hidden` and `system`.
Uses T1566.001 Spearphishing Attachment: Mustang Panda has used spearphishing attachments to deliver initial access payloads. Mustang Panda has also delivered archive files such as RAR and ZIP files containing legitimate EXEs and malicious DLLs.
Uses T1566.002 Spearphishing Link: Mustang Panda has delivered malicious links to their intended targets. Mustang Panda has distributed spear-phishing emails with embedded links that direct the victim to a malicious archive hosted on Google or Dropbox.
Uses T1567.002 Exfiltration to Cloud Storage: Mustang Panda has also exfiltrated archived files to cloud services such as Dropbox using `curl`.

title: ATT&CK Group G0129: Mustang Panda
text:
ATT&CK Group G0129: Mustang Panda
Uses T1572 Protocol Tunneling: Mustang Panda has leveraged OpenSSH (sshd.exe) to execute commands, transfer files and spread across the environment communicating over SMB port 445.
Uses T1573.001 Symmetric Cryptography: Mustang Panda has encrypted C2 communications with RC4. Mustang Panda has also leveraged encryption and compression algorithms to obfuscate the traffic between the system and C2 server, methods observed included RC4, AES, XOR with 0x5a, and LZO.
Uses T1574.001 DLL: Mustang Panda has used a legitimately signed executable to execute a malicious payload within a DLL file. Mustang Panda has abused legitimate executables to side-load malicious DLLs.
Uses T1574.005 Executable Installer File Permissions Weakness: Mustang Panda has leveraged legitimate software installer executables such as Setup Factory “IRSetup.exe” to drop and execute their payload.
Uses T1583.001 Domains: Mustang Panda has acquired C2 domains prior to operations.
Uses T1583.006 Web Services: Mustang Panda has set up Dropbox and Google Drive to host malicious downloads.
Uses T1585.002 Email Accounts: Mustang Panda has leveraged the legitimate email marketing service SMTP2Go for phishing campaigns. Mustang Panda has also created fake Google accounts to distribute malware via spear-phishing emails. Mustang Panda has also created accounts for spearphishing operations including the use of …
Uses T1586.002 Email Accounts: Mustang Panda has compromised legitimate email accounts to use in their spear-phishing operations.
Uses T1587.001 Malware: Mustang Panda has developed custom malware for use in their operations.
Uses T1588.002 Tool: Mustang Panda has obtained and leveraged publicly-available tools for intrusion activities.
Uses T1588.003 Code Signing Certificates: Mustang Panda has used revoked code signing certificates for its malicious payloads.
Uses T1588.004 Digital Certificates: Mustang Panda has obtained SSL certificates for their C2 domains.

title: ATT&CK Group G0129: Mustang Panda
text:
ATT&CK Group G0129: Mustang Panda
Uses T1593 Search Open Websites/Domains: Mustang Panda has used open-source research to identify information about victims to use in targeting to include creating weaponized phishing lures and attachments.
Uses T1598.003 Spearphishing Link: Mustang Panda has delivered web bugs to profile their intended targets.
Uses T1608 Stage Capabilities: Mustang Panda has used servers under their control to validate tracking pixels sent to phishing victims.
Uses T1608.001 Upload Malware: Mustang Panda has hosted malicious payloads on DropBox including PlugX.
Uses T1622 Debugger Evasion: Mustang Panda has embedded debug strings with messages to distract analysts. Mustang Panda has also made calls to Windows API `CheckRemoteDebuggerPresent` and exits if it detects a debugger.
Uses T1654 Log Enumeration: Mustang Panda has used Wevtutil to gather Windows Security Event Logs.
Uses T1678 Delay Execution: Mustang Panda has delayed the execution of payloads leveraging ping echo requests `cmd /c ping 8.8.8.8 -n 70&&"%temp%\<legitimate executable>"`.

title: ATT&CK Group G1004: LAPSUS$
text:
ATT&CK Group G1004: LAPSUS$
Associated names: DEV-0537, Strawberry Tempest.
LAPSUS$ is cyber criminal threat group that has been active since at least mid-2021. LAPSUS$ specializes in large-scale social engineering and extortion operations, including destructive attacks without the use of ransomware. The group has targeted organizations globally, including in the government, manufacturing, higher education, energy, healthcare, technology, telecommunications, and media sectors.
Uses T1003.003 NTDS: LAPSUS$ has used Windows built-in tool `ntdsutil` to extract the Active Directory (AD) database.
Uses T1003.006 DCSync: LAPSUS$ has used DCSync attacks to gather credentials for privilege escalation routines.
Uses T1005 Data from Local System: LAPSUS$ uploaded sensitive files, information, and credentials from a targeted organization for extortion or public release.
Uses T1068 Exploitation for Privilege Escalation: LAPSUS$ has exploited unpatched vulnerabilities on internally accessible servers including JIRA, GitLab, and Confluence for privilege escalation.
Uses T1069.002 Domain Groups: LAPSUS$ has used the AD Explorer tool to enumerate groups on a victim's network.
Uses T1078 Valid Accounts: LAPSUS$ has used compromised credentials and/or session tokens to gain access into a victim's VPN, VDI, RDP, and IAMs.
Uses T1078.004 Cloud Accounts: LAPSUS$ has used compromised credentials to access cloud assets within a target organization.
Uses T1087.002 Domain Account: LAPSUS$ has used the AD Explorer tool to enumerate users on a victim's network.
Uses T1090 Proxy: LAPSUS$ has leverage NordVPN for its egress points when targeting intended victims.
Uses T1098.003 Additional Cloud Roles: LAPSUS$ has added the global admin role to accounts they have created in the targeted organization's cloud instances.
Uses T1111 Multi-Factor Authentication Interception: LAPSUS$ has replayed stolen session token and passwords to trigger simple-approval MFA prompts in hope of the legitimate user will grant necessary approval.

title: ATT&CK Group G1004: LAPSUS$
text:
ATT&CK Group G1004: LAPSUS$
Uses T1114.003 Email Forwarding Rule: LAPSUS$ has set an Office 365 tenant level mail transport rule to send all mail in and out of the targeted organization to the newly created account.
Uses T1133 External Remote Services: LAPSUS$ has gained access to internet-facing systems and applications, including virtual private network (VPN), remote desktop protocol (RDP), and virtual desktop infrastructure (VDI) including Citrix.
Uses T1136.003 Cloud Account: LAPSUS$ has created global admin accounts in the targeted organization's cloud instances to gain persistence.
Uses T1199 Trusted Relationship: LAPSUS$ has accessed internet-facing identity providers such as Azure Active Directory and Okta to target specific organizations.
Uses T1204 User Execution: LAPSUS$ has recruited target organization employees or contractors who provide credentials and approve an associated MFA prompt, or install remote management software onto a corporate workstation, allowing LAPSUS$ to take control of an authenticated system.
Uses T1213.001 Confluence: LAPSUS$ has searched a victim's network for collaboration platforms like Confluence and JIRA to discover further high-privilege account credentials.
Uses T1213.002 Sharepoint: LAPSUS$ has searched a victim's network for collaboration platforms like SharePoint to discover further high-privilege account credentials.
Uses T1213.003 Code Repositories: LAPSUS$ has searched a victim's network for code repositories like GitLab and GitHub to discover further high-privilege account credentials.
Uses T1213.005 Messaging Applications: LAPSUS$ has searched a victim's network for organization collaboration channels like MS Teams or Slack to discover further high-privilege account credentials.
Uses T1485 Data Destruction: LAPSUS$ has deleted the target's systems and resources both on-premises and in the cloud.
Uses T1489 Service Stop: LAPSUS$ has shut down virtual machines from within a victim's on-premise VMware ESXi infrastructure.
Uses T1531 Account Access Removal: LAPSUS$ has removed a targeted organization's global admin accounts to lock the organization out of all access.

title: ATT&CK Group G1004: LAPSUS$
text:
ATT&CK Group G1004: LAPSUS$
Uses T1552.008 Chat Messages: LAPSUS$ has targeted various collaboration tools like Slack, Teams, JIRA, Confluence, and others to hunt for exposed credentials to support privilege escalation and lateral movement.
Uses T1555.003 Credentials from Web Browsers: LAPSUS$ has obtained passwords and session tokens with the use of the Redline password stealer.
Uses T1555.005 Password Managers: LAPSUS$ has accessed local password managers and databases to obtain further credentials from a compromised network.
Uses T1578.002 Create Cloud Instance: LAPSUS$ has created new virtual machines within the target's cloud environment after leveraging credential access to cloud assets.
Uses T1578.003 Delete Cloud Instance: LAPSUS$ has deleted the target's systems and resources in the cloud to trigger the organization's incident and crisis response process.
Uses T1583.003 Virtual Private Server: LAPSUS$ has used VPS hosting providers for infrastructure.
Uses T1584.002 DNS Server: LAPSUS$ has reconfigured a victim's DNS records to actor-controlled domains and websites.
Uses T1586.002 Email Accounts: LAPSUS$ has payed employees, suppliers, and business partners of target organizations for credentials.
Uses T1588.001 Malware: LAPSUS$ acquired and used the Redline password stealer in their operations.
Uses T1588.002 Tool: LAPSUS$ has obtained tools such as RVTools and AD Explorer for their operations.
Uses T1589 Gather Victim Identity Information: LAPSUS$ has gathered detailed information of target employees to enhance their social engineering lures.
Uses T1589.001 Credentials: LAPSUS$ has gathered user identities and credentials to gain initial access to a victim's organization; the group has also called an organization's help desk to reset a target's credentials.
Uses T1589.002 Email Addresses: LAPSUS$ has gathered employee email addresses, including personal accounts, for social engineering and initial access efforts.
Uses T1591.002 Business Relationships: LAPSUS$ has gathered detailed knowledge of an organization's supply chain relationships.

title: ATT&CK Group G1004: LAPSUS$
text:
ATT&CK Group G1004: LAPSUS$
Uses T1591.004 Identify Roles: LAPSUS$ has gathered detailed knowledge of team structures within a target organization.
Uses T1593.003 Code Repositories: LAPSUS$ has searched public code repositories for exposed credentials.
Uses T1597.002 Purchase Technical Data: LAPSUS$ has purchased credentials and session tokens from criminal underground forums.
Uses T1598.004 Spearphishing Voice: LAPSUS$ has called victims' help desk to convince the support personnel to reset a privileged account’s credentials.
Uses T1621 Multi-Factor Authentication Request Generation: LAPSUS$ has spammed target users with MFA prompts in the hope that the legitimate user will grant necessary approval.
Uses T1656 Impersonation: LAPSUS$ has called victims' help desk and impersonated legitimate users with previously gathered information in order to gain access to privileged accounts.

title: ATT&CK Group G0114: Chimera
text:
ATT&CK Group G0114: Chimera
Chimera is a suspected China-based threat group that has been active since at least 2018 targeting the semiconductor industry in Taiwan as well as data from the airline industry.
Uses T1003.003 NTDS: Chimera has gathered the SYSTEM registry and ntds.dit files from target systems. Chimera specifically has used the NtdsAudit tool to dump the password hashes of domain users via msadcs.exe "NTDS.dit" -s "SYSTEM" -p RecordedTV_pdmp.txt --users-csv RecordedTV_users.csv and used ntdsutil to …
Uses T1007 System Service Discovery: Chimera has used net start and net use for system service discovery.
Uses T1012 Query Registry: Chimera has queried Registry keys using reg query \\<host>\HKU\<SID>\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Terminal Server Client\Servers and reg query \\<host>\HKU\<SID>\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Internet Settings.
Uses T1016 System Network Configuration Discovery: Chimera has used ipconfig, Ping, and tracert to enumerate the IP address and network environment and settings of the local host.
Uses T1018 Remote System Discovery: Chimera has utilized various scans and queries to find domain controllers and remote services in the target environment.
Uses T1021.001 Remote Desktop Protocol: Chimera has used RDP to access targeted systems.
Uses T1021.002 SMB/Windows Admin Shares: Chimera has used Windows admin shares to move laterally.
Uses T1021.006 Windows Remote Management: Chimera has used WinRM for lateral movement.
Uses T1027.010 Command Obfuscation: Chimera has encoded PowerShell commands.
Uses T1033 System Owner/User Discovery: Chimera has used the quser command to show currently logged on users.
Uses T1036.005 Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location: Chimera has renamed malware to GoogleUpdate.exe and WinRAR to jucheck.exe, RecordedTV.ms, teredo.tmp, update.exe, and msadcs1.exe.
Uses T1039 Data from Network Shared Drive: Chimera has collected data of interest from network shares.
Uses T1041 Exfiltration Over C2 Channel: Chimera has used Cobalt Strike C2 beacons for data exfiltration.

title: ATT&CK Group G0114: Chimera
text:
ATT&CK Group G0114: Chimera
Uses T1046 Network Service Discovery: Chimera has used the get -b <start ip> -e <end ip> -p command for network scanning as well as a custom Python tool packed into a Windows executable named Get.exe to scan IP ranges for HTTP.
Uses T1047 Windows Management Instrumentation: Chimera has used WMIC to execute remote commands.
Uses T1049 System Network Connections Discovery: Chimera has used netstat -ano | findstr EST to discover network connections.
Uses T1053.005 Scheduled Task: Chimera has used scheduled tasks to invoke Cobalt Strike including through batch script schtasks /create /ru "SYSTEM" /tn "update" /tr "cmd /c c:\windows\temp\update.bat" /sc once /f /st and to maintain persistence.
Uses T1057 Process Discovery: Chimera has used tasklist to enumerate processes.
Uses T1059.001 PowerShell: Chimera has used PowerShell scripts to execute malicious payloads and the DSInternals PowerShell module to make use of Active Directory features.
Uses T1059.003 Windows Command Shell: Chimera has used the Windows Command Shell and batch scripts for execution on compromised hosts.
Uses T1069.001 Local Groups: Chimera has used net localgroup administrators to identify accounts with local administrative rights.
Uses T1070.001 Clear Windows Event Logs: Chimera has cleared event logs on compromised hosts.
Uses T1070.004 File Deletion: Chimera has performed file deletion to evade detection.
Uses T1070.006 Timestomp: Chimera has used a Windows version of the Linux touch command to modify the date and time stamp on DLLs.
Uses T1071.001 Web Protocols: Chimera has used HTTPS for C2 communications.
Uses T1071.004 DNS: Chimera has used Cobalt Strike to encapsulate C2 in DNS traffic.
Uses T1074.001 Local Data Staging: Chimera has staged stolen data locally on compromised hosts.
Uses T1074.002 Remote Data Staging: Chimera has staged stolen data on designated servers in the target environment.

title: ATT&CK Group G0114: Chimera
text:
ATT&CK Group G0114: Chimera
Uses T1078 Valid Accounts: Chimera has used a valid account to maintain persistence via scheduled task.
Uses T1078.002 Domain Accounts: Chimera has used compromised domain accounts to gain access to the target environment.
Uses T1083 File and Directory Discovery: Chimera has utilized multiple commands to identify data of interest in file and directory listings.
Uses T1087.001 Local Account: Chimera has used net user for account discovery.
Uses T1087.002 Domain Account: Chimera has has used net user /dom and net user Administrator to enumerate domain accounts including administrator accounts.
Uses T1105 Ingress Tool Transfer: Chimera has remotely copied tools and malware onto targeted systems.
Uses T1106 Native API: Chimera has used direct Windows system calls by leveraging Dumpert.
Uses T1110.003 Password Spraying: Chimera has used multiple password spraying attacks against victim's remote services to obtain valid user and administrator accounts.
Uses T1110.004 Credential Stuffing: Chimera has used credential stuffing against victim's remote services to obtain valid accounts.
Uses T1111 Multi-Factor Authentication Interception: Chimera has registered alternate phone numbers for compromised users to intercept 2FA codes sent via SMS.
Uses T1114.001 Local Email Collection: Chimera has harvested data from victim's e-mail including through execution of wmic /node:<ip> process call create "cmd /c copy c:\Users\<username>\<path>\backup.pst c:\windows\temp\backup.pst" copy "i:\<path>\<username>\My Documents\<filename>.pst" copy.
Uses T1114.002 Remote Email Collection: Chimera has harvested data from remote mailboxes including through execution of \\<hostname>\c$\Users\<username>\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Outlook*.ost.
Uses T1119 Automated Collection: Chimera has used custom DLLs for continuous retrieval of data from memory.
Uses T1124 System Time Discovery: Chimera has used time /t and net time \\ip/hostname for system time discovery.
Uses T1133 External Remote Services: Chimera has used legitimate credentials to login to an external VPN, Citrix, SSH, and other remote services.

title: ATT&CK Group G0114: Chimera
text:
ATT&CK Group G0114: Chimera
Uses T1135 Network Share Discovery: Chimera has used net share and net view to identify network shares of interest.
Uses T1201 Password Policy Discovery: Chimera has used the NtdsAudit utility to collect information related to accounts and passwords.
Uses T1213.002 Sharepoint: Chimera has collected documents from the victim's SharePoint.
Uses T1217 Browser Information Discovery: Chimera has used type \\<hostname>\c$\Users\<username>\Favorites\Links\Bookmarks bar\Imported From IE\*citrix* for bookmark discovery.
Uses T1482 Domain Trust Discovery: Chimera has nltest /domain_trusts to identify domain trust relationships.
Uses T1550.002 Pass the Hash: Chimera has dumped password hashes for use in pass the hash authentication attacks.
Uses T1556.001 Domain Controller Authentication: Chimera's malware has altered the NTLM authentication program on domain controllers to allow Chimera to login without a valid credential.
Uses T1560.001 Archive via Utility: Chimera has used gzip for Linux OS and a modified RAR software to archive data on Windows hosts.
Uses T1567.002 Exfiltration to Cloud Storage: Chimera has exfiltrated stolen data to OneDrive accounts.
Uses T1569.002 Service Execution: Chimera has used PsExec to deploy beacons on compromised systems.
Uses T1570 Lateral Tool Transfer: Chimera has copied tools between compromised hosts using SMB.
Uses T1572 Protocol Tunneling: Chimera has encapsulated Cobalt Strike's C2 protocol in DNS and HTTPS.
Uses T1574.001 DLL: Chimera has used side loading to place malicious DLLs in memory.
Uses T1588.002 Tool: Chimera has obtained and used tools such as BloodHound, Cobalt Strike, Mimikatz, and PsExec.
Uses T1589.001 Credentials: Chimera has collected credentials for the target organization from previous breaches for use in brute force attacks.
Uses T1680 Local Storage Discovery: Chimera has used `fsutil fsinfo drives`, `systeminfo`, and `vssadmin list shadows` for system information including shadow volumes and drive information.

title: ATT&CK Group G1018: TA2541
text:
ATT&CK Group G1018: TA2541
TA2541 is a cybercriminal group that has been targeting the aviation, aerospace, transportation, manufacturing, and defense industries since at least 2017. TA2541 campaigns are typically high volume and involve the use of commodity remote access tools obfuscated by crypters and themes related to aviation, transportation, and travel.
Uses T1016.001 Internet Connection Discovery: TA2541 has run scripts to check internet connectivity from compromised hosts.
Uses T1027.002 Software Packing: TA2541 has used a.NET packer to obfuscate malicious files.
Uses T1027.013 Encrypted/Encoded File: TA2541 has used compressed and char-encoded scripts in operations.
Uses T1027.015 Compression: TA2541 has used compressed and char-encoded scripts in operations.
Uses T1036.005 Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location: TA2541 has used file names to mimic legitimate Windows files or system functionality.
Uses T1047 Windows Management Instrumentation: TA2541 has used WMI to query targeted systems for security products.
Uses T1053.005 Scheduled Task: TA2541 has used scheduled tasks to establish persistence for installed tools.
Uses T1055 Process Injection: TA2541 has injected malicious code into legitimate.NET related processes including regsvcs.exe, msbuild.exe, and installutil.exe.
Uses T1055.012 Process Hollowing: TA2541 has used process hollowing to execute CyberGate malware.
Uses T1059.001 PowerShell: TA2541 has used PowerShell to download files and to inject into various Windows processes.
Uses T1059.005 Visual Basic: TA2541 has used VBS files to execute or establish persistence for additional payloads, often using file names consistent with email themes or mimicking system functionality.
Uses T1082 System Information Discovery: TA2541 has collected system information prior to downloading malware on the targeted host.
Uses T1105 Ingress Tool Transfer: TA2541 has used malicious scripts and macros with the ability to download additional payloads.
Uses T1204.001 Malicious Link: TA2541 has used malicious links to cloud and web services to gain execution on victim machines.

title: ATT&CK Group G1018: TA2541
text:
ATT&CK Group G1018: TA2541
Uses T1204.002 Malicious File: TA2541 has used macro-enabled MS Word documents to lure victims into executing malicious payloads.
Uses T1218.005 Mshta: TA2541 has used `mshta` to execute scripts including VBS.
Uses T1518.001 Security Software Discovery: TA2541 has used tools to search victim systems for security products such as antivirus and firewall software.
Uses T1547.001 Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder: TA2541 has placed VBS files in the Startup folder and used Registry run keys to establish persistence for malicious payloads.
Uses T1562.001 Disable or Modify Tools: TA2541 has attempted to disable built-in security protections such as Windows AMSI.
Uses T1566.001 Spearphishing Attachment: TA2541 has sent phishing emails with malicious attachments for initial access including MS Word documents.
Uses T1566.002 Spearphishing Link: TA2541 has used spearphishing e-mails with malicious links to deliver malware.
Uses T1568 Dynamic Resolution: TA2541 has used dynamic DNS services for C2 infrastructure.
Uses T1573.002 Asymmetric Cryptography: TA2541 has used TLS encrypted C2 communications including for campaigns using AsyncRAT.
Uses T1583.001 Domains: TA2541 has registered domains often containing the keywords “kimjoy,” “h0pe,” and “grace,” using domain registrars including Netdorm and No-IP DDNS, and hosting providers including xTom GmbH and Danilenko, Artyom.
Uses T1583.006 Web Services: TA2541 has hosted malicious files on various platforms including Google Drive, OneDrive, Discord, PasteText, ShareText, and GitHub.
Uses T1588.001 Malware: TA2541 has used multiple strains of malware available for purchase on criminal forums or in open-source repositories.
Uses T1588.002 Tool: TA2541 has used commodity remote access tools.
Uses T1608.001 Upload Malware: TA2541 has uploaded malware to various platforms including Google Drive, Pastetext, Sharetext, and GitHub.

title: ATT&CK Group G1022: ToddyCat
text:
ATT&CK Group G1022: ToddyCat
ToddyCat is a sophisticated threat group that has been active since at least 2020 using custom loaders and malware in multi-stage infection chains against government and military targets across Europe and Asia.
Uses T1005 Data from Local System: ToddyCat has run scripts to collect documents from targeted hosts.
Uses T1018 Remote System Discovery: ToddyCat has used `ping %REMOTE_HOST%` for post exploit discovery.
Uses T1021.002 SMB/Windows Admin Shares: ToddyCat has used locally mounted network shares for lateral movement through targated environments.
Uses T1036.005 Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location: ToddyCat has used the name `debug.exe` for malware components.
Uses T1047 Windows Management Instrumentation: ToddyCat has used WMI to execute scripts for post exploit document collection.
Uses T1049 System Network Connections Discovery: ToddyCat has used `netstat -anop tcp` to discover TCP connections to compromised hosts.
Uses T1053.005 Scheduled Task: ToddyCat has used scheduled tasks to execute discovery commands and scripts for collection.
Uses T1057 Process Discovery: ToddyCat has run `cmd /c start /b tasklist` to enumerate processes.
Uses T1059.001 PowerShell: ToddyCat has used Powershell scripts to perform post exploit collection.
Uses T1059.003 Windows Command Shell: ToddyCat has used.bat scripts and `cmd` for execution on compromised hosts.
Uses T1069.002 Domain Groups: ToddyCat has executed `net group "domain admins" /dom` for discovery on compromised machines.
Uses T1074.002 Remote Data Staging: ToddyCat manually transferred collected files to an exfiltration host using xcopy.
Uses T1078.002 Domain Accounts: ToddyCat has used compromised domain admin credentials to mount local network shares.
Uses T1083 File and Directory Discovery: ToddyCat has run scripts to enumerate recently modified documents having either a.pdf,.doc,.docx,.xls or.xlsx extension.
Uses T1087.002 Domain Account: ToddyCat has run `net user %USER% /dom` for account discovery.
Uses T1095 Non-Application Layer Protocol: ToddyCat has used a passive backdoor that receives commands with UDP packets.

title: ATT&CK Group G1022: ToddyCat
text:
ATT&CK Group G1022: ToddyCat
Uses T1106 Native API: ToddyCat has used `WinExec` to execute commands received from C2 on compromised hosts.
Uses T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application: ToddyCat has exploited the ProxyLogon vulnerability (CVE-2021-26855) to compromise Exchange Servers at multiple organizations.
Uses T1518.001 Security Software Discovery: ToddyCat can determine is Kaspersky software is running on an endpoint by running `cmd /c wmic process where name="avp.exe"`.
Uses T1560.001 Archive via Utility: ToddyCat has leveraged xcopy, 7zip, and RAR to stage and compress collected documents prior to exfiltration.
Uses T1562.004 Disable or Modify System Firewall: Prior to executing a backdoor ToddyCat has run `cmd /c start /b netsh advfirewall firewall add rule name="SGAccessInboundRule" dir=in protocol=udp action=allow localport=49683` to allow the targeted system to receive UDP packets on port 49683.
Uses T1564.003 Hidden Window: ToddyCat has hidden malicious scripts using `powershell.exe -windowstyle hidden`.
Uses T1566.003 Spearphishing via Service: ToddyCat has sent loaders configured to run Ninja as zip archives via Telegram.
Uses T1567.002 Exfiltration to Cloud Storage: ToddyCat has used a DropBox uploader to exfiltrate stolen files.
Uses T1680 Local Storage Discovery: ToddyCat has collected information on bootable drives including model, vendor, and serial numbers.

title: ATT&CK Group G1002: BITTER
text:
ATT&CK Group G1002: BITTER
Associated names: T-APT-17.
BITTER is a suspected South Asian cyber espionage threat group that has been active since at least 2013. BITTER has targeted government, energy, and engineering organizations in Pakistan, China, Bangladesh, and Saudi Arabia.
Uses T1027.013 Encrypted/Encoded File: BITTER has used a RAR SFX dropper to deliver malware.
Uses T1036.004 Masquerade Task or Service: BITTER has disguised malware as a Windows Security update service.
Uses T1053.005 Scheduled Task: BITTER has used scheduled tasks for persistence and execution.
Uses T1068 Exploitation for Privilege Escalation: BITTER has exploited CVE-2021-1732 for privilege escalation.
Uses T1071.001 Web Protocols: BITTER has used HTTP POST requests for C2.
Uses T1095 Non-Application Layer Protocol: BITTER has used TCP for C2 communications.
Uses T1105 Ingress Tool Transfer: BITTER has downloaded additional malware and tools onto a compromised host.
Uses T1203 Exploitation for Client Execution: BITTER has exploited Microsoft Office vulnerabilities CVE-2012-0158, CVE-2017-11882, CVE-2018-0798, and CVE-2018-0802.
Uses T1204.002 Malicious File: BITTER has attempted to lure victims into opening malicious attachments delivered via spearphishing.
Uses T1559.002 Dynamic Data Exchange: BITTER has executed OLE objects using Microsoft Equation Editor to download and run malicious payloads.
Uses T1566.001 Spearphishing Attachment: BITTER has sent spearphishing emails with a malicious RTF document or Excel spreadsheet.
Uses T1568 Dynamic Resolution: BITTER has used DDNS for C2 communications.
Uses T1573 Encrypted Channel: BITTER has encrypted their C2 communications.
Uses T1583.001 Domains: BITTER has registered a variety of domains to host malicious payloads and for C2.
Uses T1588.002 Tool: BITTER has obtained tools such as PuTTY for use in their operations.
Uses T1608.001 Upload Malware: BITTER has registered domains to stage payloads.

title: ATT&CK Group G0048: RTM
text:
ATT&CK Group G0048: RTM
RTM is a cybercriminal group that has been active since at least 2015 and is primarily interested in users of remote banking systems in Russia and neighboring countries. The group uses a Trojan by the same name (RTM).
Uses T1102.001 Dead Drop Resolver: RTM has used an RSS feed on Livejournal to update a list of encrypted C2 server names.
Uses T1189 Drive-by Compromise: RTM has distributed its malware via the RIG and SUNDOWN exploit kits, as well as online advertising network Yandex.Direct.
Uses T1204.002 Malicious File: RTM has attempted to lure victims into opening e-mail attachments to execute malicious code.
Uses T1219.002 Remote Desktop Software: RTM has used a modified version of TeamViewer and Remote Utilities for remote access.
Uses T1547.001 Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder: RTM has used Registry run keys to establish persistence for the RTM Trojan and other tools, such as a modified version of TeamViewer remote desktop software.
Uses T1566.001 Spearphishing Attachment: RTM has used spearphishing attachments to distribute its malware.
Uses T1574.001 DLL: RTM has used search order hijacking to force TeamViewer to load a malicious DLL.

title: ATT&CK Group G0045: menuPass
text:
ATT&CK Group G0045: menuPass
Associated names: Cicada, POTASSIUM, Stone Panda, APT10, Red Apollo, CVNX, HOGFISH, BRONZE RIVERSIDE.
menuPass is a threat group that has been active since at least 2006. Individual members of menuPass are known to have acted in association with the Chinese Ministry of State Security's (MSS) Tianjin State Security Bureau and worked for the Huaying Haitai Science and Technology Development Company.

menuPass has targeted healthcare, defense, aerospace, finance, maritime, biotechnology, energy, and government sectors globally, with an emphasis on Japanese organizations. In 2016 and 2017, the group is known to have targeted managed IT service providers (MSPs), manufacturing and mining companies, and a university.
Uses T1003.002 Security Account Manager: menuPass has used a modified version of pentesting tools wmiexec.vbs and secretsdump.py to dump credentials.
Uses T1003.003 NTDS: menuPass has used Ntdsutil to dump credentials.
Uses T1003.004 LSA Secrets: menuPass has used a modified version of pentesting tools wmiexec.vbs and secretsdump.py to dump credentials.
Uses T1005 Data from Local System: menuPass has collected various files from the compromised computers.
Uses T1016 System Network Configuration Discovery: menuPass has used several tools to scan for open NetBIOS nameservers and enumerate NetBIOS sessions.
Uses T1018 Remote System Discovery: menuPass uses scripts to enumerate IP ranges on the victim network. menuPass has also issued the command net view /domain to a PlugX implant to gather information about remote systems on the network.
Uses T1021.001 Remote Desktop Protocol: menuPass has used RDP connections to move across the victim network.
Uses T1021.004 SSH: menuPass has used Putty Secure Copy Client (PSCP) to transfer data.
Uses T1027.013 Encrypted/Encoded File: menuPass has encoded strings in its malware with base64 as well as with a simple, single-byte XOR obfuscation using key 0x40.

title: ATT&CK Group G0045: menuPass
text:
ATT&CK Group G0045: menuPass
Uses T1036 Masquerading: menuPass has used esentutl to change file extensions to their true type that were masquerading as.txt files.
Uses T1036.003 Rename Legitimate Utilities: menuPass has renamed certutil and moved it to a different location on the system to avoid detection based on use of the tool.
Uses T1036.005 Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location: menuPass has been seen changing malicious files to appear legitimate.
Uses T1039 Data from Network Shared Drive: menuPass has collected data from remote systems by mounting network shares with net use and using Robocopy to transfer data.
Uses T1046 Network Service Discovery: menuPass has used tcping.exe, similar to Ping, to probe port status on systems of interest.
Uses T1047 Windows Management Instrumentation: menuPass has used a modified version of pentesting script wmiexec.vbs, which logs into a remote machine using WMI.
Uses T1049 System Network Connections Discovery: menuPass has used net use to conduct connectivity checks to machines.
Uses T1053.005 Scheduled Task: menuPass has used a script (atexec.py) to execute a command on a target machine via Task Scheduler.
Uses T1055.012 Process Hollowing: menuPass has used process hollowing in iexplore.exe to load the RedLeaves implant.
Uses T1056.001 Keylogging: menuPass has used key loggers to steal usernames and passwords.
Uses T1059.001 PowerShell: menuPass uses PowerSploit to inject shellcode into PowerShell.
Uses T1059.003 Windows Command Shell: menuPass executes commands using a command-line interface and reverse shell. The group has used a modified version of pentesting script wmiexec.vbs to execute commands. menuPass has used malicious macros embedded inside Office documents to execute files.
Uses T1070.003 Clear Command History: menuPass has used Wevtutil to remove PowerShell execution logs.
Uses T1070.004 File Deletion: A menuPass macro deletes files after it has decoded and decompressed them.

title: ATT&CK Group G0045: menuPass
text:
ATT&CK Group G0045: menuPass
Uses T1074.001 Local Data Staging: menuPass stages data prior to exfiltration in multi-part archives, often saved in the Recycle Bin.
Uses T1074.002 Remote Data Staging: menuPass has staged data on remote MSP systems or other victim networks prior to exfiltration.
Uses T1078 Valid Accounts: menuPass has used valid accounts including shared between Managed Service Providers and clients to move between the two environments.
Uses T1083 File and Directory Discovery: menuPass has searched compromised systems for folders of interest including those related to HR, audit and expense, and meeting memos.
Uses T1087.002 Domain Account: menuPass has used the Microsoft administration tool csvde.exe to export Active Directory data.
Uses T1090.002 External Proxy: menuPass has used a global service provider's IP as a proxy for C2 traffic from a victim.
Uses T1105 Ingress Tool Transfer: menuPass has installed updates and new malware on victims.
Uses T1106 Native API: menuPass has used native APIs including GetModuleFileName, lstrcat, CreateFile, and ReadFile.
Uses T1119 Automated Collection: menuPass has used the Csvde tool to collect Active Directory files and data.
Uses T1140 Deobfuscate/Decode Files or Information: menuPass has used certutil in a macro to decode base64-encoded content contained in a dropper document attached to an email. The group has also used certutil -decode to decode files on the victim’s machine when dropping UPPERCUT.
Uses T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application: menuPass has leveraged vulnerabilities in Pulse Secure VPNs to hijack sessions.
Uses T1199 Trusted Relationship: menuPass has used legitimate access granted to Managed Service Providers in order to access victims of interest.
Uses T1204.002 Malicious File: menuPass has attempted to get victims to open malicious files such as Windows Shortcuts (.lnk) and/or Microsoft Office documents, sent via email as part of spearphishing campaigns.

title: ATT&CK Group G0045: menuPass
text:
ATT&CK Group G0045: menuPass
Uses T1210 Exploitation of Remote Services: menuPass has used tools to exploit the ZeroLogon vulnerability (CVE-2020-1472).
Uses T1218.004 InstallUtil: menuPass has used InstallUtil.exe to execute malicious software.
Uses T1553.002 Code Signing: menuPass has resized and added data to the certificate table to enable the signing of modified files with legitimate signatures.
Uses T1560 Archive Collected Data: menuPass has encrypted files and information before exfiltration.
Uses T1560.001 Archive via Utility: menuPass has compressed files before exfiltration using TAR and RAR.
Uses T1566.001 Spearphishing Attachment: menuPass has sent malicious Office documents via email as part of spearphishing campaigns as well as executables disguised as documents.
Uses T1568.001 Fast Flux DNS: menuPass has used dynamic DNS service providers to host malicious domains.
Uses T1574.001 DLL: menuPass has used DLL side-loading to launch versions of Mimikatz and PwDump6 as well as UPPERCUT. menuPass has also used DLL search order hijacking.
Uses T1583.001 Domains: menuPass has registered malicious domains for use in intrusion campaigns.
Uses T1588.002 Tool: menuPass has used and modified open-source tools like Impacket, Mimikatz, and pwdump.

title: ATT&CK Group G1053: Storm-0501
text:
ATT&CK Group G1053: Storm-0501
Storm-0501 is a financially motivated cyber criminal group that uses commodity and open-source tools to conduct ransomware operations. Storm-0501 has been active since 2021 and has previously been affiliated with Sabbath Ransomware and other Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) variants such as Hive, BlackCat, Hunters International, LockBit 3.0, and Embargo ransomware.
Uses T1003 OS Credential Dumping: Storm-0501 has used the SecretsDump module within Impacket can perform credential dumping to obtain account and password information.
Uses T1003.006 DCSync: Storm-0501 has utilized DCSync to extract credentials from victims.
Uses T1021.006 Windows Remote Management: Storm-0501 has utilized the post-exploitation tool known as Evil-WinRM that uses PowerShell over Windows Remote Management (WinRM) for remote code execution.
Uses T1021.007 Cloud Services: Storm-0501 has used compromised Entra Connect Sync Server to move laterally within the victim environment.
Uses T1027.002 Software Packing: Storm-0501 has used Themida to pack Cobalt Strike payloads.
Uses T1036.004 Masquerade Task or Service: Storm-0501 has utilized Rclone masqueraded as svhost.exe and scvhost.exe.
Uses T1053.005 Scheduled Task: Storm-0501 had used a scheduled task named “SysUpdate” that was registered via GPO on devices in the network to distribute the Embargo ransomware.
Uses T1057 Process Discovery: Storm-0501 has discovered running processes through `tasklist.exe`.
Uses T1059.001 PowerShell: Storm-0501 has leveraged PowerShell to execute commands and scripts.
Uses T1059.009 Cloud API: Storm-0501 has leveraged Cloud CLI to execute commands and exfiltrate data from compromised environments.
Uses T1078.004 Cloud Accounts: Storm-0501 has leveraged compromised accounts to access Microsoft Entra Connect, which was used to synchronize on-premises identities and Microsoft Entra identities, allowing users to sign into both environments with the same password. Storm-0501 has also used the victim Global Administrator …

title: ATT&CK Group G1053: Storm-0501
text:
ATT&CK Group G1053: Storm-0501
Uses T1082 System Information Discovery: Storm-0501 has leveraged native Windows tools and commands such as `systeminfo` and open-source tools including OSQuery and ossec-win32 to query details about the endpoint.
Uses T1087.002 Domain Account: Storm-0501 has utilized an obfuscated version of the Active Directory reconnaissance tool ADRecon.ps1 (obfs.ps1 or recon.ps1) to discover domain accounts.
Uses T1087.004 Cloud Account: Storm-0501 has conducted enumeration of users, roles, and resources within victim Azure tenants using the tool Azurehound.
Uses T1098.001 Additional Cloud Credentials: Storm-0501 has reset the password of identified administrator accounts that lack MFA and registered their own MFA method.
Uses T1098.003 Additional Cloud Roles: Storm-0501 has elevated their access to Azure resources using `Microsoft.Authorization/elevateAccess/action` and `Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write` operations to gain User Access Administrator and Owner Azure roles over the victims’ Azure subscriptions.
Uses T1110 Brute Force: Storm-0501 has leveraged brute force attacks to obtain credentials.
Uses T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application: Storm-0501 has exploited N-day vulnerabilities associated with public facing services to gain initial access to victim environments to include Zoho ManageEngine (CVE-2022-47966), Citrix NetScaler “Citrix Bleed” (CVE-2023-4966), and Adobe ColdFusion 2016 (CVE-2023-29300 or CVE-2023-38203).
Uses T1218.010 Regsvr32: Storm-0501 has launched Cobalt Strike Beacon files using regsvr32.exe.
Uses T1218.011 Rundll32: Storm-0501 has launched Cobalt Strike Beacon files with rundll32.exe.
Uses T1219.002 Remote Desktop Software: Storm-0501 has used legitimate remote monitoring and management (RMM) tools including AnyDesk, NinjaOne, and Level.io.
Uses T1482 Domain Trust Discovery: Storm-0501 has used Windows native utility Nltest `nltest.exe` for discovery.
Uses T1484.001 Group Policy Modification: Storm-0501 distributed Group Policy Objects to tamper with security products.
Uses T1484.002 Trust Modification: Storm-0501 created a new federated domain within the victim Microsoft Entra tenant using Global Administrator level access to establish a persistent backdoor for later use.
Uses T1485 Data Destruction: Storm-0501 has destroyed data and backup files.

title: ATT&CK Group G1053: Storm-0501
text:
ATT&CK Group G1053: Storm-0501
Uses T1486 Data Encrypted for Impact: Storm-0501 has encrypted files in victim environments using ransomware as a service (RaaS) including Sabbath, Hive, BlackCat, Hunters International, LockBit 3.0 and Embargo ransomware.
Uses T1490 Inhibit System Recovery: Storm-0501 has deleted snapshots, restore points, storage accounts, and backup services to prevent remediation and restoration. Storm-0501 has also impacted Azure resources through the targeting of `Microsoft.Compute/snapshots/delete`, `Microsoft.Compute/restorePointCollections/delete`, `Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/delete`, and `Microsoft.RecoveryServices/Vaults/backupFabrics/protectionContainers/delete`.
Uses T1518.001 Security Software Discovery: Storm-0501 has detected endpoint security solutions using `sc query sense` and `sc query windefend`.
Uses T1526 Cloud Service Discovery: Storm-0501 has discovered the victim environment’s protections to include Azure policies, resource locks, and Azure Storage immutability policies.
Uses T1530 Data from Cloud Storage: Storm-0501 had modified Azure Storage account resources through the `Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/write` operation to expose non-remotely accessible accounts for data exfiltration.
Uses T1537 Transfer Data to Cloud Account: Storm-0501 has copied data from the victims environment to their own infrastructure leveraging AzCopy CLI.
Uses T1552.004 Private Keys: Storm-0501 has leveraged the Azure Owner role to access and steal the Storage Account Access keys using the `Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/listkeys/action` operation.
Uses T1555.005 Password Managers: Storm-0501 has stolen credentials contained in the password manager Keepass by utilizing Find-KeePassConfig.ps1.
Uses T1555.006 Cloud Secrets Management Stores: Storm-0501 has utilized Azure Key Vault to store the encryption key using the operation `Microsoft.KeyVault/Vaults/write`.
Uses T1556.009 Conditional Access Policies: Storm-0501 has registered their own MFA method, and leveraged a victim hybrid joined server to circumvent Conditional Access Policies.
Uses T1567.002 Exfiltration to Cloud Storage: Storm-0501 has exfiltrated stolen data to the MEGA file sharing site. Storm-0501 has also utilized Rclone to exfiltrate data from victim environments to cloud storage such as MegaSync. Storm-0501 has exfiltrated data to their own infrastructure utilizing AzCopy Command-Line tool …

title: ATT&CK Group G1053: Storm-0501
text:
ATT&CK Group G1053: Storm-0501
Uses T1578.003 Delete Cloud Instance: Storm-0501 has conducted mass deletion of cloud data stores and resources from Azure subscriptions.
Uses T1580 Cloud Infrastructure Discovery: Storm-0501 has enumerated compromised cloud environments to identify critical assets, data stores, and back resources.
Uses T1587.003 Digital Certificates: Storm-0501 has utilized their own self-signed TLS certificate “Microsoft IT TLS CA 5” with their infrastructure.
Uses T1588.006 Vulnerabilities: Storm-0501 has obtained capabilities to exploit N-day vulnerabilities associated with public facing services to gain initial access to victim environments to include Zoho ManageEngine (CVE-2022-47966), Citrix NetScaler “Citrix Bleed” (CVE-2023-4966), and Adobe ColdFusion 2016 (CVE-2023-29300 or CVE-2023-38203).
Uses T1614.001 System Language Discovery: Storm-0501 has identified system language codes on a compromised host to determine if the victim falls under a non-supported language code that is prohibited for targeting, including victims associated with Russia and other Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) that may …
Uses T1657 Financial Theft: Storm-0501 has engaged in double-extortion ransomware, exfiltrating data and directly contacting victims when the primary organization refuses to pay along with posting data on their data leak sites.

title: ATT&CK Group G0081: Tropic Trooper
text:
ATT&CK Group G0081: Tropic Trooper
Associated names: Pirate Panda, KeyBoy.
Tropic Trooper is an unaffiliated threat group that has led targeted campaigns against targets in Taiwan, the Philippines, and Hong Kong. Tropic Trooper focuses on targeting government, healthcare, transportation, and high-tech industries and has been active since 2011.
Uses T1016 System Network Configuration Discovery: Tropic Trooper has used scripts to collect the host's network topology.
Uses T1020 Automated Exfiltration: Tropic Trooper has used a copy function to automatically exfiltrate sensitive data from air-gapped systems using USB storage.
Uses T1027.003 Steganography: Tropic Trooper has used JPG files with encrypted payloads to mask their backdoor routines and evade detection.
Uses T1027.013 Encrypted/Encoded File: Tropic Trooper has encrypted configuration files.
Uses T1033 System Owner/User Discovery: Tropic Trooper used letmein to scan for saved usernames on the target system.
Uses T1036.005 Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location: Tropic Trooper has hidden payloads in Flash directories and fake installer files.
Uses T1046 Network Service Discovery: Tropic Trooper used pr and an openly available tool to scan for open ports on target systems.
Uses T1049 System Network Connections Discovery: Tropic Trooper has tested if the localhost network is available and other connection capability on an infected system using command scripts.
Uses T1052.001 Exfiltration over USB: Tropic Trooper has exfiltrated data using USB storage devices.
Uses T1055.001 Dynamic-link Library Injection: Tropic Trooper has injected a DLL backdoor into dllhost.exe and svchost.exe.
Uses T1057 Process Discovery: Tropic Trooper is capable of enumerating the running processes on the system using pslist.
Uses T1059.003 Windows Command Shell: Tropic Trooper has used Windows command scripts.
Uses T1070.004 File Deletion: Tropic Trooper has deleted dropper files on an infected system using command scripts.
Uses T1071.001 Web Protocols: Tropic Trooper has used HTTP in communication with the C2.

title: ATT&CK Group G0081: Tropic Trooper
text:
ATT&CK Group G0081: Tropic Trooper
Uses T1071.004 DNS: Tropic Trooper's backdoor has communicated to the C2 over the DNS protocol.
Uses T1078.003 Local Accounts: Tropic Trooper has used known administrator account credentials to execute the backdoor directly.
Uses T1082 System Information Discovery: Tropic Trooper has detected a target system’s OS version.
Uses T1083 File and Directory Discovery: Tropic Trooper has monitored files' modified time.
Uses T1091 Replication Through Removable Media: Tropic Trooper has attempted to transfer USBferry from an infected USB device by copying an Autorun function to the target machine.
Uses T1105 Ingress Tool Transfer: Tropic Trooper has used a delivered trojan to download additional files.
Uses T1106 Native API: Tropic Trooper has used multiple Windows APIs including HttpInitialize, HttpCreateHttpHandle, and HttpAddUrl.
Uses T1119 Automated Collection: Tropic Trooper has collected information automatically using the adversary's USBferry attack.
Uses T1132.001 Standard Encoding: Tropic Trooper has used base64 encoding to hide command strings delivered from the C2.
Uses T1135 Network Share Discovery: Tropic Trooper used netview to scan target systems for shared resources.
Uses T1140 Deobfuscate/Decode Files or Information: Tropic Trooper used shellcode with an XOR algorithm to decrypt a payload. Tropic Trooper also decrypted image files which contained a payload.
Uses T1203 Exploitation for Client Execution: Tropic Trooper has executed commands through Microsoft security vulnerabilities, including CVE-2017-11882, CVE-2018-0802, and CVE-2012-0158.
Uses T1204.002 Malicious File: Tropic Trooper has lured victims into executing malware via malicious e-mail attachments.
Uses T1221 Template Injection: Tropic Trooper delivered malicious documents with the XLSX extension, typically used by OpenXML documents, but the file itself was actually an OLE (XLS) document.
Uses T1505.003 Web Shell: Tropic Trooper has started a web service in the target host and wait for the adversary to connect, acting as a web shell.

title: ATT&CK Group G0081: Tropic Trooper
text:
ATT&CK Group G0081: Tropic Trooper
Uses T1518 Software Discovery: Tropic Trooper's backdoor could list the infected system's installed software.
Uses T1518.001 Security Software Discovery: Tropic Trooper can search for anti-virus software running on the system.
Uses T1543.003 Windows Service: Tropic Trooper has installed a service pointing to a malicious DLL dropped to disk.
Uses T1547.001 Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder: Tropic Trooper has created shortcuts in the Startup folder to establish persistence.
Uses T1547.004 Winlogon Helper DLL: Tropic Trooper has created the Registry key HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon\Shell and sets the value to establish persistence.
Uses T1564.001 Hidden Files and Directories: Tropic Trooper has created a hidden directory under C:\ProgramData\Apple\Updates\ and C:\Users\Public\Documents\Flash\.
Uses T1566.001 Spearphishing Attachment: Tropic Trooper sent spearphishing emails that contained malicious Microsoft Office and fake installer file attachments.
Uses T1573 Encrypted Channel: Tropic Trooper has encrypted traffic with the C2 to prevent network detection.
Uses T1573.002 Asymmetric Cryptography: Tropic Trooper has used SSL to connect to C2 servers.
Uses T1574.001 DLL: Tropic Trooper has been known to side-load DLLs using a valid version of a Windows Address Book and Windows Defender executable with one of their tools.
Uses T1680 Local Storage Discovery: Tropic Trooper has detected a target system’s system volume information.

title: ATT&CK Group G1020: Mustard Tempest
text:
ATT&CK Group G1020: Mustard Tempest
Associated names: DEV-0206, TA569, GOLD PRELUDE, UNC1543.
Mustard Tempest is an initial access broker that has operated the SocGholish distribution network since at least 2017. Mustard Tempest has partnered with Indrik Spider to provide access for the download of additional malware including LockBit, WastedLocker, and remote access tools.
Uses T1036.005 Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location: Mustard Tempest has used the filename `AutoUpdater.js` to mimic legitimate update files and has also used the Cyrillic homoglyph characters С `(0xd0a1)` and а `(0xd0b0)`, to produce the filename `Сhrome.Updаte.zip`.
Uses T1082 System Information Discovery: Mustard Tempest has used implants to perform system reconnaissance on targeted systems.
Uses T1105 Ingress Tool Transfer: Mustard Tempest has deployed secondary payloads and third stage implants to compromised hosts.
Uses T1189 Drive-by Compromise: Mustard Tempest has used drive-by downloads for initial infection, often using fake browser updates as a lure.
Uses T1204.001 Malicious Link: Mustard Tempest has lured users into downloading malware through malicious links in fake advertisements and spearphishing emails.
Uses T1566.002 Spearphishing Link: Mustard Tempest has sent victims emails containing links to compromised websites.
Uses T1583.004 Server: Mustard Tempest has acquired servers to host second-stage payloads that remain active for a period of either days, weeks, or months.
Uses T1583.008 Malvertising: Mustard Tempest has posted false advertisements including for software packages and browser updates in order to distribute malware.
Uses T1584.001 Domains: Mustard Tempest operates a global network of compromised websites that redirect into a traffic distribution system (TDS) to select victims for a fake browser update page.
Uses T1608.001 Upload Malware: Mustard Tempest has hosted payloads on acquired second-stage servers for periods of either days, weeks, or months.
Uses T1608.004 Drive-by Target: Mustard Tempest has injected malicious JavaScript into compromised websites to infect victims via drive-by download.

title: ATT&CK Group G1020: Mustard Tempest
text:
ATT&CK Group G1020: Mustard Tempest
Uses T1608.006 SEO Poisoning: Mustard Tempest has poisoned search engine results to return fake software updates in order to distribute malware.

title: ATT&CK Group G0073: APT19
text:
ATT&CK Group G0073: APT19
Associated names: Codoso, C0d0so0, Codoso Team, Sunshop Group.
APT19 is a Chinese-based threat group that has targeted a variety of industries, including defense, finance, energy, pharmaceutical, telecommunications, high tech, education, manufacturing, and legal services. In 2017, a phishing campaign was used to target seven law and investment firms. Some analysts track APT19 and Deep Panda as the same group, but it is unclear from open source information if the groups are the same.
Uses T1016 System Network Configuration Discovery: APT19 used an HTTP malware variant and a Port 22 malware variant to collect the MAC address and IP address from the victim’s machine.
Uses T1027.010 Command Obfuscation: APT19 used Base64 to obfuscate executed commands.
Uses T1027.013 Encrypted/Encoded File: APT19 used Base64 to obfuscate payloads.
Uses T1033 System Owner/User Discovery: APT19 used an HTTP malware variant and a Port 22 malware variant to collect the victim’s username.
Uses T1059 Command and Scripting Interpreter: APT19 downloaded and launched code within a SCT file.
Uses T1059.001 PowerShell: APT19 used PowerShell commands to execute payloads.
Uses T1071.001 Web Protocols: APT19 used HTTP for C2 communications. APT19 also used an HTTP malware variant to communicate over HTTP for C2.
Uses T1082 System Information Discovery: APT19 collected system architecture information. APT19 used an HTTP malware variant and a Port 22 malware variant to gather the hostname and CPU information from the victim’s machine.
Uses T1112 Modify Registry: APT19 uses a Port 22 malware variant to modify several Registry keys.
Uses T1132.001 Standard Encoding: An APT19 HTTP malware variant used Base64 to encode communications to the C2 server.
Uses T1140 Deobfuscate/Decode Files or Information: An APT19 HTTP malware variant decrypts strings using single-byte XOR keys.
Uses T1189 Drive-by Compromise: APT19 performed a watering hole attack on forbes.com in 2014 to compromise targets.

title: ATT&CK Group G0073: APT19
text:
ATT&CK Group G0073: APT19
Uses T1204.002 Malicious File: APT19 attempted to get users to launch malicious attachments delivered via spearphishing emails.
Uses T1218.010 Regsvr32: APT19 used Regsvr32 to bypass application control techniques.
Uses T1218.011 Rundll32: APT19 configured its payload to inject into the rundll32.exe.
Uses T1543.003 Windows Service: An APT19 Port 22 malware variant registers itself as a service.
Uses T1547.001 Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder: An APT19 HTTP malware variant establishes persistence by setting the Registry key HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run\Windows Debug Tools-%LOCALAPPDATA%\.
Uses T1564.003 Hidden Window: APT19 used -W Hidden to conceal PowerShell windows by setting the WindowStyle parameter to hidden.
Uses T1566.001 Spearphishing Attachment: APT19 sent spearphishing emails with malicious attachments in RTF and XLSM formats to deliver initial exploits.
Uses T1574.001 DLL: APT19 launched an HTTP malware variant and a Port 22 malware variant using a legitimate executable that loaded the malicious DLL.
Uses T1588.002 Tool: APT19 has obtained and used publicly-available tools like Empire.

title: ATT&CK Group G1009: Moses Staff
text:
ATT&CK Group G1009: Moses Staff
Associated names: DEV-0500, Marigold Sandstorm.
Moses Staff is a suspected Iranian threat group that has primarily targeted Israeli companies since at least September 2021. Moses Staff openly stated their motivation in attacking Israeli companies is to cause damage by leaking stolen sensitive data and encrypting the victim's networks without a ransom demand. 

Security researchers assess Moses Staff is politically motivated, and has targeted government, finance, travel, energy, manufacturing, and utility companies outside of Israel as well, including those in Italy, India, Germany, Chile, Turkey, the UAE, and the US.
Uses T1016 System Network Configuration Discovery: Moses Staff has collected the domain name of a compromised network.
Uses T1021.002 SMB/Windows Admin Shares: Moses Staff has used batch scripts that can enable SMB on a compromised host.
Uses T1027.013 Encrypted/Encoded File: Moses Staff has used obfuscated web shells in their operations.
Uses T1082 System Information Discovery: Moses Staff collected information about the infected host, including the machine names and OS architecture.
Uses T1087.001 Local Account: Moses Staff has collected the administrator username from a compromised host.
Uses T1105 Ingress Tool Transfer: Moses Staff has downloaded and installed web shells to following path C:\inetpub\wwwroot\aspnet_client\system_web\IISpool.aspx.
Uses T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application: Moses Staff has exploited known vulnerabilities in public-facing infrastructure such as Microsoft Exchange Servers.
Uses T1505.003 Web Shell: Moses Staff has dropped a web shell onto a compromised system.
Uses T1553.002 Code Signing: Moses Staff has used signed drivers from an open source tool called DiskCryptor to evade detection.
Uses T1562.004 Disable or Modify System Firewall: Moses Staff has used batch scripts that can disable the Windows firewall on specific remote machines.
Uses T1587.001 Malware: Moses Staff has built malware, such as DCSrv and PyDCrypt, for targeting victims' machines.

title: ATT&CK Group G1009: Moses Staff
text:
ATT&CK Group G1009: Moses Staff
Uses T1588.002 Tool: Moses Staff has used the commercial tool DiskCryptor.

title: ATT&CK Group G0021: Molerats
text:
ATT&CK Group G0021: Molerats
Associated names: Operation Molerats, Gaza Cybergang.
Molerats is an Arabic-speaking, politically-motivated threat group that has been operating since 2012. The group's victims have primarily been in the Middle East, Europe, and the United States.
Uses T1027.015 Compression: Molerats has delivered compressed executables within ZIP files to victims.
Uses T1053.005 Scheduled Task: Molerats has created scheduled tasks to persistently run VBScripts.
Uses T1057 Process Discovery: Molerats actors obtained a list of active processes on the victim and sent them to C2 servers.
Uses T1059.001 PowerShell: Molerats used PowerShell implants on target machines.
Uses T1059.005 Visual Basic: Molerats used various implants, including those built with VBScript, on target machines.
Uses T1059.007 JavaScript: Molerats used various implants, including those built with JS, on target machines.
Uses T1105 Ingress Tool Transfer: Molerats used executables to download malicious files from different sources.
Uses T1140 Deobfuscate/Decode Files or Information: Molerats decompresses ZIP files once on the victim machine.
Uses T1204.001 Malicious Link: Molerats has sent malicious links via email trick users into opening a RAR archive and running an executable.
Uses T1204.002 Malicious File: Molerats has sent malicious files via email that tricked users into clicking Enable Content to run an embedded macro and to download malicious archives.
Uses T1218.007 Msiexec: Molerats has used msiexec.exe to execute an MSI payload.
Uses T1547.001 Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder: Molerats saved malicious files within the AppData and Startup folders to maintain persistence.
Uses T1553.002 Code Signing: Molerats has used forged Microsoft code-signing certificates on malware.
Uses T1555.003 Credentials from Web Browsers: Molerats used the public tool BrowserPasswordDump10 to dump passwords saved in browsers on victims.
Uses T1566.001 Spearphishing Attachment: Molerats has sent phishing emails with malicious Microsoft Word and PDF attachments.

title: ATT&CK Group G0021: Molerats
text:
ATT&CK Group G0021: Molerats
Uses T1566.002 Spearphishing Link: Molerats has sent phishing emails with malicious links included.

title: ATT&CK Group G0038: Stealth Falcon
text:
ATT&CK Group G0038: Stealth Falcon
Stealth Falcon is a threat group that has conducted targeted spyware attacks against Emirati journalists, activists, and dissidents since at least 2012. Circumstantial evidence suggests there could be a link between this group and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) government, but that has not been confirmed.
Uses T1005 Data from Local System: Stealth Falcon malware gathers data from the local victim system.
Uses T1012 Query Registry: Stealth Falcon malware attempts to determine the installed version of.NET by querying the Registry.
Uses T1016 System Network Configuration Discovery: Stealth Falcon malware gathers the Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) table from the victim.
Uses T1033 System Owner/User Discovery: Stealth Falcon malware gathers the registered user and primary owner name via WMI.
Uses T1041 Exfiltration Over C2 Channel: After data is collected by Stealth Falcon malware, it is exfiltrated over the existing C2 channel.
Uses T1047 Windows Management Instrumentation: Stealth Falcon malware gathers system information via Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI).
Uses T1053.005 Scheduled Task: Stealth Falcon malware creates a scheduled task entitled “IE Web Cache” to execute a malicious file hourly.
Uses T1057 Process Discovery: Stealth Falcon malware gathers a list of running processes.
Uses T1059 Command and Scripting Interpreter: Stealth Falcon malware uses WMI to script data collection and command execution on the victim.
Uses T1059.001 PowerShell: Stealth Falcon malware uses PowerShell commands to perform various functions, including gathering system information via WMI and executing commands from its C2 server.
Uses T1071.001 Web Protocols: Stealth Falcon malware communicates with its C2 server via HTTPS.
Uses T1082 System Information Discovery: Stealth Falcon malware gathers system information via WMI, including the system directory, build number, serial number, version, manufacturer, model, and total physical memory.

title: ATT&CK Group G0038: Stealth Falcon
text:
ATT&CK Group G0038: Stealth Falcon
